Deterministic counts of what happened on a local calendar day in
the active workspace (CON-285): posts published (by channel),
failed/not-published (by channel + per-post detail), created (by
author) and campaigns created. Computed server-side, so tz is
required. A future or empty day returns a zeroed 200.

Non-empty days newest-first (CON-285), keyset-paginated by date
via `before`. Each item carries the four headline totals — enough
for a feed row without fetching each day's detail.

post.description:
Sends an instruction to the Campaign Assistant and streams progress via Server-Sent Events.
"explanation_delta" carries {"delta":"..."} fragments as the reply streams. "tool_call"/"tool_result"
signal tool invocations. When a content plan runs, "content_plan_started", "content_plan_post"
(etc.) and "content_plan_complete" are forwarded; when the brief is enriched, "enrich_brief_started",
the per-field "enrich_brief_*_delta" events and "enrich_brief_complete" are forwarded. A final
"complete" event carries the CampaignAssistantResponse. "error" carries {"message":"...","code":<http_code>}.
Available to any user in the campaign's tenant.

200.description: SSE stream: delta / tool_call / tool_result / *_complete / complete / error events

post.description:
Read-only review of the brief's internal consistency and
completeness (CON-116). Streams step / complete / error events.
Does not modify the brief. Available to any user in the tenant.
post.summary: Review the campaign brief for consistency (SSE)

200.description: SSE stream: step / complete / error events

post.description:
Improves the campaign brief (description, target persona, key messages, tone guidelines),
streaming progress via Server-Sent Events. A non-empty brief is edited in place, keeping its
subject and honouring its tone guidelines and the brand voice; an empty brief is drafted
from the campaign's title and type. The optional instruction says what to change.
Per-field "*_delta" events preview each value as it is written; a final "complete"
event carries the full EnrichBriefResponse and is the signal that the brief is ready.
On failure an "error" event carries {"message":"<text>","code":<http_code>}.
The brief is returned as a suggestion only — it is not persisted to the campaign.

200.description: SSE stream: step / *_delta / complete / error events

post.description:
Calls the AI content plan flow and streams progress via Server-Sent Events.
Each step emits an SSE event of type "step" with payload {"step":"<name>","status":"done"}.
On success a final "complete" event carries the full ContentPlanResponse payload.
On failure an "error" event carries {"message":"<text>","code":<http_code>}.

200.description: SSE stream: step / complete / error events

post.description:
Generates a few new draft posts for a platform subset, a single
phase, and a publish-date window (CON-114). Streams the same
step / post / warning / complete / error events as generate-draft.
Available to any user in the campaign's tenant.

200.description: SSE stream: step / post / warning / complete / error events

get.description:
Returns the most recent Campaign Assistant conversation messages for a campaign.
A "model" message's content is the JSON of that turn's "complete" event: action,
explanation and the tool results (brief, briefReview with findings, contentPlan,
generatedPosts, draftedPosts, dates, redistribute, postsReview).

Returns the per-campaign overview projection (CON-113): a plain
tenant-scoped DB read, available to any user in the tenant.

Returns each phase of the campaign's type with its inclusive date window and post count (CON-166).
With no stored plan the windows are derived: the campaign's start/end dates split evenly across
the phases (remainder days to the earliest) — the same windows content generation uses.
source is "unscheduled" (and the dates null) while the campaign has no dates.

put.description:
Replaces the campaign's phase windows with a manual plan (CON-166). The plan must hold exactly one
window per phase of the campaign's type, contiguous in phase order (each starts the day after the
previous ends — no gaps or overlaps), the first starting on start_date and the last ending on
end_date. Content generation then plans posts into these windows. 400 invalid_phase_plan names
the first offending phase; 409 campaign_unscheduled when the campaign has no dates.

delete.description:
Drops the campaign's manual phase plan so the windows are derived from its dates again (CON-166).
Idempotent. Returns the resulting (derived) plan.

post.description:

Step 3 of 3: confirms the PUT object (size + 5 GiB cap), then enqueues the first transcription run atomically. Idempotent (deterministic run_key). The asset then moves `pending` → `processing` → `ready`/`partial`/`failed`; poll `GET /{id}/audio`. On completion the transcript becomes the asset's `content` and time-anchored chunks (`GET /{id}/chunks`).
Gated by the media_storage_bytes tier limit on the uploaded size (402 `entitlement_exceeded`).

parameters.description: Asset to finalize (+ optional model pin)

post.description:
Step 1 of 3 of audio ingestion (CON-282): mints a pending `AUDIO` asset and returns a 30-minute presigned PUT. The client PUTs the bytes straight to object storage with the returned `method` + `headers` (the Content-Type is bound into the signature), then calls `POST /audio/finalize`. Accepted: mp3, wav, m4a, aac, ogg/oga, opus, flac, webm, aif/aiff (max 5 GiB, enforced at finalize).
Gated by the content_bank_assets tier limit (402 `entitlement_exceeded`).

Adds and/or removes tag IDs on many assets in one call — the
filing operation the Content Bank's multi-select needs (CON-279),
where you tag many documents at once. Each listed asset keeps the
tags it already has, minus `remove`, plus `add`; the result is
deduped and preserves order. Assets outside the caller's tenant
are skipped. Returns the updated assets with tags hydrated.

Accepts one or more files under the field `files`, routed by extension. Files are processed independently — one failure does not block others; each gets a result with `status` `created` or `failed`.
- `.md` (max 10 MB): converted to BlockNote JSON synchronously (`MD`, `ready`).
- `.pdf` (max 50 MB): stored, then processed asynchronously (text extraction, page-aware chunking, embedding, thumbnail) as `PDF` (`pending` → `ready`/`partial`/`failed`).
- Images — JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, HEIC/HEIF, AVIF, TIFF, BMP (operator-set cap, default 50 MB; SVG is rejected): stored and ingested asynchronously by image-service (normalize, EXIF-strip, vision description, region extraction, alt text) as `IMG` (`pending` → `ready`/`partial`/`failed`); deduplicated within the tenant by checksum. Poll `GET /{id}/image` for the run.
- Office/text documents — .docx/.docm/.dotx, .xlsx/.xlsm/.xltx, .pptx/.pptm/.potx, .odt/.ods/.odp (+ flat), .epub, .csv/.tsv, .html/.xhtml, .eml, .rtf, .txt/.log (max 50 MB; legacy/password-protected OLE2 rejected): parsed asynchronously by document-service into source-anchored chunks as `DOC` (`pending` → `ready`/`partial`/`failed`, with `failure_code`/`failure_reason` on the asset when failed).
Audio is not accepted here — use `POST /audio/presign` + `/audio/finalize`.
A failed result carries a stable `code` beside the prose `error`: `extension_not_allowed`, `unsupported_media_type`, `vector_rejected`, `too_large`, `empty_file`, `invalid_file`, `dimensions_exceeded`, `quota_exceeded` (content-bank asset or media-storage tier limit), `service_unavailable`, `internal_error`. Match on the code; fall back to the prose for unknown codes.

post.description: Scrapes a web page to Markdown (with mirrored images) via Firecrawl and persists it as a URL asset (CON-222). Re-submitting the same URL refreshes the existing asset in place (200) instead of duplicating it (201).

IMG content is the image description — may be empty; an edit re-embeds it together with the stored region chunks. PDF/DOC/AUDIO content is ingestion output and read-only: send it unchanged or omit it (empty = keep); a different value is a 409 `{code: "content_locked"}` — re-extract instead. Renaming an ingested asset never re-chunks it.
`alt_text_edited_by_user` flips to true only when alt_text actually changes.

get.description:
Subscribes the authenticated user to a long-lived
Server-Sent Events stream filtered by topic patterns.

Topic filters are passed via the `topics` query param as a
comma-separated list. Supported forms per filter:
- "all"               — receive every event the user is
authorised to see.
- "kind:id"           — exact match (e.g. "entity:post:Xq").
- "kind:*"            — prefix wildcard (e.g. "job:*").

Each event is emitted as one SSE frame:
id: <event-id>
event: <type>
data: <json>

A heartbeat comment (`: ping`) is sent every 20 seconds.
Delivery is at-most-once; the server holds no event log.
Subscribers are disconnected if their per-connection buffer
overflows (the client should reconnect and reconcile via REST).

`post.attachments.changed` on `entity:post:<id>` follows every
committed attachment write: upload, video finalize, attach from
the content bank or an integration (Figma plugin), update,
reorder, delete, and generated alt text landing. Its data is a
refetch hint, never attachment data or URLs:
`{post_id, attachment_id, action, source}`, where action is
created|updated|reordered|deleted (attachment_id is empty for
reordered) and source is editor|bank|figma_plugin|alt_text.
Every member of the workspace receives it, including the actor.

The `Last-Event-ID` request header is currently accepted
and ignored — reserved for future replay support.

get.description:
Long-lived Server-Sent Events stream of the caller's
notifications. On connect the server replays everything created
after the client's cursor (Last-Event-ID header, or ?since=)
from the durable log, then switches to live push — so a client
that was offline during a burst misses nothing. A fresh client
(no cursor) goes live-only and catches history via the REST list.

Each notification is one frame: `id: <seq>` / `event:
notification` / `data: <json>`. A heartbeat comment (`: ping`)
is sent every 20 seconds.

post.description: Always answers 202, whether or not the address has an account, and in the same latency envelope — the response never reveals whether an account exists (CON-161). On a hit it emails a single-use reset link; on a miss it does nothing.

`post_id`, `event_type`, `actor`, `since`/`until`

Returns all posts ordered by creation date, with campaign, platform, and assets hydrated.

post.description:
Creates a new post. The created_by field is set from the authenticated session.
The `content` field is a Markdown string; the frontend renders it via BlockNote.
`platform_id` and `platform_post_type` are required only when `status` is not `draft`;
drafts can be saved without a platform chosen up front.

Converts a set of posts — or every scheduled post for a
platform — from auto-publish (`scheduled`) to
`scheduled_for_manual_publishing`, keeping `scheduled_at`.
Each post's live Zernio job is cancelled server-side by a
cancel_zernio_job task, which then lands the post directly
on `scheduled_for_manual_publishing` — no detour through
`ready_for_publish`, so the post is never left unscheduled
if the client disconnects mid-flight. Returns per-post
outcomes: `converted` (accepted / already manual) and
`failed` (not found, or not in a convertible state). A
post that publishes before its cancel lands is handled by
the worker and recorded in the Post Log (CON-130).
post.summary: Convert scheduled posts to manual publishing

post.description:
Splits a single authored body into thread segments (manual "---"
delimiters, else auto-split by the platform's per-segment limit)
and validates them exactly as the publish gate will. Stateless.

get.description: Returns a single post by Sqid with campaign, platform, and assets hydrated.

put.description:
Replaces all mutable fields of an existing post.
The `content` field is a Markdown string; the frontend renders it via BlockNote.
`platform_id` and `platform_post_type` are required only when the new `status` is
not `draft`; transitioning a draft to `ready_for_publish` (or beyond) without a
platform chosen returns 400.

409.description: Submitted content locked, or code use_cancel_endpoint: a scheduled post can only leave scheduled via POST /cancel or /convert-to-manual, and its date and account can't change; or code schedule_changed: it was cancelled or published while the edit was in flight

delete.description:
Deletes a post by Sqid. A scheduled post's copy queued in Zernio is withdrawn,
so it no longer publishes. A published post can't be deleted (409 post_published):
it is live on the network and anchors its analytics.

get.description: Returns the latest engagement snapshot for a post published through a publisher. Served entirely from the database — never live-calls the publisher (CON-93 FR4). Two 200 shapes: a full snapshot, or — when the background refresh has not yet covered the post — the pending form `{"status":"pending","post_id":"..."}` so clients can poll. Both are covered by the schema below (the snapshot fields are absent on the pending response; `status` is absent on a snapshot).

post.description:
Runs the Post quality assessment agent (CON-85) and streams
Server-Sent Events: a "step" event per flow stage, then a
final "complete" event carrying the persisted evaluation
(four 0-10 dimension scores with rationale, weakness, and
span-anchored suggestions, plus the backend-computed overall).

get.description:
Returns the most recent persisted quality evaluation for a
post (CON-85/CON-92) without invoking the model. The frontend
reads this to render an existing assessment and only triggers
POST /assess when the post has changed since it was scored.

post.description:
Unions the given asset ids into the post's sources
(posts.used_asset_ids), touching no other field. The write is a
single atomic UPDATE, so concurrent attaches of different sources
both survive and omitted fields are never reset (CON-233).
Adding an already-present id is a no-op. A source change to a
submitted post (scheduled/published) is content-locked (409),
mirroring PUT (CON-251). Returns the updated post.
post.summary: Attach source assets to a post

delete.description:
Removes one asset id from the post's sources
(posts.used_asset_ids), touching no other field (CON-233).
Removing an id that is not present is a no-op. Detaching a source
from a submitted post (scheduled/published) is content-locked
(409), mirroring PUT (CON-251). Returns the updated post.
delete.summary: Detach a source asset from a post

post.description:
Sends an instruction to the AI assistant and streams progress via Server-Sent Events.
Events: "explanation_delta" and "content_delta" carry {"delta":"..."} fragments (Markdown)
as the model generates the explanation and updated content. "tool_call" and "tool_result"
signal asset-retrieval tool invocations. "complete" carries the final PostAssistantResponse
whose updatedContent is a Markdown string.
"error" carries {"message":"...","code":<http_code>}.

200.description: SSE stream: delta / tool_call / tool_result / complete / error events

post.description:
Enqueues a River cancel_zernio_job task. The Post
remains in `Scheduled` until Zernio confirms the
cancellation; on confirmation it transitions to the
requested target (`ready_for_publish` or `draft`).
If Zernio reports the job has already been published
(race), the cancellation is a no-op and the next poll
cycle lands `Published` per the normal success path
(CON-69 §9).

Duplicates a post as a new draft in the same campaign and phase, copying
title, content, media/attachments, used assets, CTA, and audience notes.
Attachments are deep-copied in object storage so the clone is independent
of its source. Pass target_platform_id/target_post_type to retarget the
clone (verbatim content — the assistant path adapts content for you).

get.description: Returns the most recent assistant conversation messages for a post.

post.description:
Restore is non-destructive: the target version's content is
copied into a brand-new version that becomes the new HEAD, so
the full history is preserved and the restore is itself
reversible. If the live post has unsnapshotted edits, they are
auto-saved as a version first so nothing is lost. Restoring to
the version that already matches the current content is a no-op.

Schedules a `ready_for_publish` post for the given absolute
time (CON-78). Allowlisted platforms route to `scheduled`
(auto-publish, Zernio submit enqueued); others route to
`scheduled_for_manual_publishing`. Pass `allow_promote` to
auto-promote a `draft` (runs CON-74 pre-publish validation,
then Draft → ReadyForPublish) before scheduling. The status
change, `scheduled_at`, audit entries, and Zernio enqueue
commit in one transaction.
Confirms a manually-published post exists on the platform via Zernio sync-external, back-fills its publisher linkage + permalink, marks it published, and records a first analytics snapshot (CON-153).

get.description: Returns all version snapshots for a post.

get.description:
Returns the post's attachments ordered by position, with a
soft pre-check (`platform_validation`) per CON-73 §2.4 that
surfaces any rule failure for the post's current target
platform. Each attachment carries a short-lived presigned
GET URL when object storage is configured.

post.description:
Accepts a single image (CON-73) or PDF (CON-75) file via
multipart/form-data under the field `file`. Images — JPEG,
PNG, WebP, GIF, HEIC/HEIF, AVIF, TIFF, BMP — are validated and
EXIF-stripped (pixels preserved) by image-service (CON-281);
SVG is rejected. PDFs are validated as application/pdf and
get a best-effort first-page PNG thumbnail. Video uses the
presign flow instead. Caps are operator-set (defaults: 50 MB
images, 100 MB PDFs) and the upload counts toward the
tenant's media_storage_bytes tier limit (402 when over).
Per-platform caps are surfaced as soft warnings in the
response. A reject is `{code, error}` with a stable code:
unsupported_media_type, vector_rejected, too_large,
empty_file, invalid_file, dimensions_exceeded,
service_unavailable, internal_error.

409.description: post is in a terminal publishing state

post.description:
Probes the uploaded object via video-service (duration, codec,
resolution, poster frame), validates it against the post's
platform, and persists the attachment row (CON-148). Corrupt
or unreadable video is a terminal 400; an unrecognised
container/codec is 415. If video-service is unreachable the
attachment is still created, unprobed (no duration/poster,
weaker validation). The object's real size is checked against
the media storage quota; over it, the object is deleted (402).

Creates a post attachment from an existing `IMG` asset without
re-uploading. The bank keeps the original upload (EXIF and
all), so its bytes go through the same metadata strip a direct
upload gets and land as the attachment's own object: deleting
the asset later leaves the post intact. The asset's alt text
and its user-edited flag carry over unless `alt_text` is sent;
an asset without alt text gets it generated as on upload. The
copy counts toward media_storage_bytes (402 when over).
Per-platform caps are soft warnings in the response, exactly as
on upload. Image rejects use the upload's `{code, error}` shape.
post.summary: Attach a content-bank image to a post

409.description: post is in a terminal publishing state

post.description:
Returns a short-lived PUT URL the client uses to upload video
bytes straight to object storage, bypassing the API process so
multi-GB files never buffer in memory (CON-148). The client
then calls finalize with the returned `s3_key`. Only video
content types are accepted here; images/PDFs use the direct
upload endpoint. Hard cap: 5 GiB. The declared size is checked
against the workspace's media storage quota (402 when over).

patch.description:
Renumbers the post's attachments to match `ids` (0..n-1) in one
transaction, so the whole list reorders in a single request
without tripping UNIQUE(post_id, position) (CON-124). `ids` must
list every current attachment exactly once. Returns the
reordered list.

delete.description:
Removes an attachment row and its S3 object(s). For PDF
attachments this includes the rendered thumbnail. If any

returned so the caller can retry (CON-73 §2.7).

patch.description:
Updates an attachment's `position` and/or `alt_text` (at least

registered counter, attached by the authenticated /me/entitlements
read so the client can render "N of M". Omitted (nil) for an uncounted or
boolean feature and for the public pricing catalog (no tenant) — the client
treats absent as "unknown", distinct from a real 0.

session.description:
Session is set only on the new-account path (auto-login); an existing
account is already signed in, so it accepts without a new session.

alt_text.description:
AltText is the accessibility description for the media. Empty
means "no alt text". Editable on upload and via PATCH; sent to Zernio as
mediaItems[].altText. For images it is auto-generated by image-service
unless a user has supplied/edited it (see AltTextEditedByUser).

alt_text_edited_by_user.description:
AltTextEditedByUser guards a user's alt text from being overwritten by
async auto-generation: the generator fills AltText only while
this is false; a user-supplied alt_text on upload or a PATCH sets it true.

duration_ms.description:
DurationMs and Codec carry video metadata probed by video-service.
Zero/empty for non-video attachments and when the probe
is unavailable (graceful degradation). Width/Height are reused for
the video's frame size.

presigned_url.description:
PresignedURL and ThumbnailURL are hydrated by the handler at
response time; they are not stored in the database.

segment_index.description:
SegmentIndex names which message of a threaded post this attachment
belongs to, 0-based into Post.ThreadSegments. NULL for every
attachment of a non-thread post — it belongs to the whole/single post,
today's behaviour. Within a segment, Position still orders the media. A
pointer so nil ⇔ NULL is distinct from a valid segment 0.

source.description:
Source is derived (even split of the campaign dates), manual (user-edited)
or unscheduled (the campaign has no dates, so the phases have none).

brand_voice_id.description:
Presence-aware: omitting a brand ref on a full-replace save
leaves the stored value alone; an explicit null clears it. See Optional.

goal_cadence.description:
Goal cadence: "week" | "month". Empty falls back to "month".
estimated_post_count is the target posts per one of these periods.

publishing_time.description:
Scheduling settings. All optional; omitted fields fall back to
defaults (09:00 / UTC / every day / ±15 min) via normalizeScheduling.

use_assets.description:
UseAssets / AssetIDs are presence-aware: the content-bank set has
its own membership endpoints (POST/DELETE /campaigns/:id/assets) that keep
use_assets derived from it, so an ordinary whole-record save that omits
these must leave them alone rather than restate the set (and reset the flag)
over an in-flight membership write. Present replaces; explicit null on
asset_ids clears. See Optional, applyToValue and applyOptionalSlice.

target.description:
Target is the status the user wants the post moved to once
Zernio confirms the cancellation. Defaults to "ready_for_publish"
when omitted (ReadyForPublish is the most common
"cancel and edit" landing state).

role.description: Role defaults to member; an owner may invite a co-owner by passing "owner".

Role is optional; it defaults to member. Only an owner may create users,
so an owner can also mint a co-owner by passing "owner".

model.description: PinnedModel optionally overrides the configured transcription model for this run.

accountCount.description:
AccountCount is per-tenant, so it is a pointer that stays nil (and is
omitted) on the unauthenticated/tenantless path — a bare "accountCount":0
there would falsely read as "this tenant has 0 accounts". It is set only
inside the tenant-scoped branch below, after ListActive.

has_account.description:
HasAccount tells the accept page which mode applies without a wasted POST:
true → the invited email already has an Ogen account, so prompt "sign in as
<email>" (no password field) and accept; false → collect name + password to
create the account. The invitee already holds the capability token and sees
their own email here, so disclosing whether that one address is registered
adds no meaningful enumeration surface.

before.description:
Before bounds the update to notifications the caller has actually seen
(seq <= Before), so one that arrives mid-click stays unread. 0 = all.

password.description:
min=8 mirrors signup (createUserRequest); the client additionally requires
upper/lower/digit.

connect_supported.description:
ConnectSupported records whether Ogen can OAuth-redirect connect this
platform. false documents the Bluesky-style app-password exclusion as data
rather than code.

enabled.description:
Enabled is the operator soft on/off switch. A disabled platform
drops from GET /api/platforms and blocks new connects, but already-scheduled
posts still publish (the publish path resolves zernio_id regardless).

post_type_canvases.description:
PostTypeCanvases is the recommended artwork size per media-bearing
post-type slug, surfaced on the post-type rules (composer hints, the
Figma plugin's board frames).

supported_post_types.description:
SupportedPostTypes is the Zernio-publishable subset of PostTypes' slugs
— replaces SupportedPlatform.SupportedPostTypes. PostTypes carries
every slug for display; this array marks which ones actually publish.

zernio_id.description:
ZernioID is the Zernio wire slug ("twitter", "linkedin", …). It replaces
the retired Go registry's sqidToZernioID map: the publish path
and connect flow resolve this off the row. "" means the operator has not
yet assigned a slug (the row is not publishable until they do).

posts_changed_at.description:
PostsChangedAt moves forward whenever a post is created, deleted,
moved, rescheduled, retitled, or has its platform, post type or status
changed; null if the campaign never had a post.

PostsChangedAt moves forward whenever a post is created, deleted,
moved, rescheduled, retitled, or has its platform, post type or status
changed; null if the campaign never had a post.

media.description:
Media lists the post's attachments: whole-post media first, then each
thread segment's, each by position.

platforms.description:
Platforms holds the rules of every platform one of its posts is on, by
platform id.

Platforms holds the rules of every platform a listed post is on, by
platform id.

preview_url.description:
PreviewURL is a presigned GET for a JPEG, PNG or GIF of at most 4096 px
on the long edge: the image itself, a scaled copy of it, or a video's
poster. Null for PDFs, videos without a poster, and previews that
couldn't be made.

status.description:
Status is "pending" ONLY on the no-snapshot-yet variant, where the
200 body is just {status, post_id} (the background refresh hasn't
covered this post). Omitted on a real snapshot — don't confuse it
with SyncStatus, which is the publisher sync state of an existing
snapshot. Declared here so the single Swagger 2.0 success schema
documents both 200 shapes (Swagger 2.0 allows one schema per code).

brand_voice_id.description:
BrandVoiceID / BrandAudienceID are presence-aware: unlike the
other client-authored fields on this full-replace body, these are stamped
server-side by content_plan / draft_post, so an omitted key must leave the
stored ref untouched rather than null it. See Optional and apply.

content_format.description:
ContentFormat is presence-aware so an autosave from a client that predates
the field can't wipe it: omitted leaves it alone, null clears it.

cta_type.description:
CTAType is accepted for compatibility and ignored: the stored value is
derived from CTAUrl.

cta_url.description:
CTAUrl is the link a link-post publishes. Not validated on write, so an
autosave of a half-typed URL is kept; the publish gate checks it.

first_comment.description:
FirstComment and FirstCommentDelayMinutes are presence-aware like
ContentFormat: omitted leaves them alone; a null or "" comment clears it.

platform_id.description:
PlatformID + PlatformPostType are required only when status is not
"draft" — see update.RequirePlatformIfNotDraft. Drafts can be saved
before the user has picked a platform.

published_url.description:
PublishedURL lets the front-end record a permalink for posts
Zernio cannot verify (the CON-149 skip path — e.g. LinkedIn personal
accounts) or correct a wrong one. Like every field on this whole-resource
PUT, the FE round-trips the current value; an empty string clears it.

series_id.description:
SeriesID is presence-aware like ContentFormat: omitted leaves it alone,
null clears it. It must name a live library series or one local to the
post's campaign.

social_account_id.description:
SocialAccountID names which same-platform account the post
publishes to. Optional: omit it and the submit worker auto-selects the
platform's single account, or requires a choice when there are several.

thread_segments.description:
ThreadSegments is DERIVED, not authored (R2): a thread is written
as a single body in Content (with "---" delimiter lines, or auto-split by the
per-segment char limit), and the server materialises the segment list from it.
A client-sent value here is IGNORED — the field is retained only so existing
callers that still send it don't error, and GET responses carry the derived
list back on the Post model (not this request type).

used_asset_ids.description:
UsedAssetIDs is presence-aware: the sources have their own
membership endpoints (POST/DELETE /posts/:id/assets), so an ordinary
whole-record save that omits the key must leave the stored set alone rather
than restate it and race the membership write. A present array replaces it;
an explicit null clears it. See Optional and applyOptionalSlice.

ids.description:
IDs is the post's attachments in their new order. It must list every
current attachment exactly once.

segment_index.description:
SegmentIndex reassigns which thread segment the media belongs to.
Presence-aware so the three JSON states stay distinct: absent ⇒ leave as-is,
a number ⇒ move to that segment, explicit null ⇒ detach (back to a
whole-post attachment).

current_password.description:
CurrentPassword re-authenticates a credential change: it is
required only when Password is present and is verified against the stored
hash, so it carries no min-length rule of its own. A plain name/email edit
leaves it empty and unchecked.

password.description: Password is optional on update; when provided it must be at least 8 characters.

code.description:
Code is a stable, machine-readable companion to Error on a failed result:
the client matches the code and falls back to the prose when it
is unknown. Empty on a created result. See models.UploadCode*.

reset_url.description:
ResetURL is a fresh single-use password-reset link. It is empty when the
account has no live workspace to attach a reset token to; such an account
can't sign in anyway.

alt_text.description:
AltText is a short accessibility description for image assets,
distinct from content (the longer, embeddable description). Empty for
non-image assets. For images it is auto-generated by image-service unless a
user has edited it (CON-281, see AltTextEditedByUser).

alt_text_edited_by_user.description:
AltTextEditedByUser guards a user's manual alt text from being overwritten
by (re-)processing: image-service fills AltText only while this
is false; a PUT that sets alt_text flips it true, so re-extraction never
clobbers a human edit.

failure_code.description:
FailureCode/FailureReason say why ingestion failed: a stable
models.UploadCode* plus tenant-visible prose. Set only while status is
failed; any other status write clears them. Written for DOC assets —
audio/image carry theirs on the extraction row.

images.description:
Images are the mirrored page images for URL assets, hydrated and
URL-decorated by the handler layer. Not persisted on assets.

origin.description:
Origin is where the asset came from beyond a plain upload ('' for
uploads, AssetOriginFigma for frames a Figma plugin sent); OriginRef is
the origin-specific pointer back to the source. A checksum-dedupe hit
keeps the first asset's provenance.

source_url.description:
SourceURL is the origin URL for URL-scraped assets; nil for
MD/PDF/text assets. Unique per tenant, so re-submitting a URL refreshes
the same asset instead of duplicating it.

source_anchor.description:
SourceAnchor is the structured location backing SourceLabel,
stored as jsonb. nil for non-document chunks.

source_label.description:
SourceLabel is a human-readable citation for the chunk's origin,
e.g. "Slide 4", "Sheet 'Q3 Pipeline' rows 10-24", or a heading breadcrumb.
nil for chunks that predate document ingestion (PDF/URL/MD).

normalized_s3_key.description: NormalizedS3Key points at the browser-drawable derivative image-service writes for every image (assets/{id}/normalized.png). It exists precisely so formats a browser can't decode — HEIC/HEIF, TIFF — can still be shown: url is the original bytes, this is the copy an renders. Null for PDFs and for images whose extraction failed or is still pending.

url.description:
URL, ThumbnailURL and NormalizedURL are transient public URLs rendered from
S3Key / ThumbnailS3Key / NormalizedS3Key by the handler layer before
serialization. URL is the original bytes; NormalizedURL is the copy
a browser can draw — the full-size asset screen renders it for
HEIC/TIFF; ThumbnailURL is the small preview. Not persisted; minted per
response so a signed/public URL is never stored or cached client-side.

width.description:
Width, Height, IsAnimated and ChecksumSHA256 describe image files.
Same names/types as post_attachments so the attach-to-post bridge is a
field copy. Zero/empty for PDFs. ChecksumSHA256 also backs upload dedupe.

url.description:
URL is a transient public URL rendered from S3Key by the handler layer
before serialization. Not persisted.

audio_seconds.description: AudioSeconds is the processed source duration (a usage/quota dimension).

cost_micros.description:
CostMicros is the run's transcription cost, snapshotted at write time from
the versioned gemini price table; PriceVersion records which table.

failure_code.description:
FailureCode is the stable, machine-readable companion to FailureReason
(models.UploadCode*), so the client can word it without parsing prose.

failure_reason.description:
FailureReason is a tenant-visible reason for a terminal failed/partial run
(over-duration, over-cap, unusable audio).

run_key.description:
RunKey makes an extraction idempotent: a duplicate enqueue for the same
(asset_id, run_key) hits the unique index and no-ops. A re-extract uses a
new RunKey so it is a distinct run.

cost_micros.description:
CostMicros is this segment's transcription cost, snapshotted from
the versioned gemini price table and persisted in the SAME write that marks
the segment done — so cost and completion commit atomically and a resume
that skips a done segment never loses its cost. The extraction total sums
these.

archived_at.description:
Lifecycle (CON-156 BE 6). A campaign leaves the active set by being
archived (reversible) or soft-deleted (an operational safety net, not an
undo — no self-serve restore). Both are nullable timestamps filtered
explicitly in the repository rather than via bun's soft_delete tag, so
archive and delete stay independent: GetByID still returns an archived
campaign (to unarchive it) while hiding a deleted one.

brand_voice_id.description:
Brand bindings: the voice/audience this campaign writes in.
Nullable — resolution falls back to the workspace default voice /
tone_guidelines prose when unset. FK ON DELETE SET NULL.

goal_cadence.description:
Goal. estimated_post_count above is the target number of posts
PER goal_cadence period; the content-plan flow multiplies it by the number
of week/month periods the campaign's [start_date, end_date] window spans,
and the campaign overview reports per-period progress against it.

publishing_time.description:
Scheduling settings — consumed by the content-plan flow to
place each generated draft's scheduled_at. PublishingTime is a local
"HH:MM" wall clock; Timezone is an IANA name ("" = UTC); PublishingDays
is a subset of mon..sun; SpreadMinutes is the ± jitter (0 = exact).

type_locked.description:
Phase plan. TypeLocked: campaign_type_id can no longer change
because posts are planned against the type's phases (PhasedPostCount > 0);
hydrated on reads. PhaseWindows is the stored manual phase plan, hydrated
on GetByID — empty means derived; read it via campaignphase.Resolve.
PhasePlanReset is set on a PUT response when a type/date change dropped
the manual plan back to derived.

weight.description:
Weight is the fraction (0-1) this dimension contributed to the
overall, taken from the Type weight profile. Contribution is the
weighted percentage points it added to overall_pct
(Weight * Score/10 * 100). Both are backend-computed.

created_by.description:
CreatedBy is stamped from the session on insert and never changes. It goes
null only when the author's user row is hard-deleted; CreatedByName is the
capture-time snapshot that keeps the author after that.

anchor.description:
Anchor is the image-region location (Kind == "image", a normalized bbox),
reusing the shared SourceAnchor jsonb shape.

cells.description:
Cells carries a table block's grid (row/col/text), stored as jsonb; nil for
non-table blocks.

kind.description:
Kind/Level/Text mirror a documents Block: kind is heading|paragraph|
list_item|table|composite|...; level is a heading depth (0 otherwise).

provenance.description:
Provenance is "image_extraction"; LowConfidence marks a tabular block whose
source is a screenshot rather than a source file.

blocks.description: Blocks is hydrated by the read API from image_blocks; not persisted here.

classify_model.description:
Model ids used this run (config, never compiled in). EscalateModel is only
meaningful when Escalated is true.

description_ok.description:
DescriptionOK/ExtractionOK/Truncated are the service's self-reported quality
signals; a description-ok/extraction-failed run settles to `partial`.

escalated.description:
Escalated marks a one-shot re-run at a stronger model on low confidence;
EscalationImproved records whether it actually helped (recorded regardless).

failure_code.description:
FailureCode is the stable, machine-readable companion to FailureReason
— one of models.UploadCode* — so the client can distinguish a
quota block from a bad image from a transient outage from a searchable-but-
partial run without parsing prose. Empty on a clean complete run.

failure_reason.description:
FailureReason is a tenant-visible reason for a terminal failed/partial run
(unsupported/vector, over pixel-area/size, over quota, unreadable).

input_tokens.description:
Token totals across the run's vision calls (classify + extract + describe +
alt + any escalation); CostMicros is the snapshotted price, PriceVersion the
table it came from.

run_key.description:
RunKey makes an extraction idempotent: a duplicate enqueue for the same
(asset_id, run_key) hits the unique index and no-ops. A re-extract uses a
new RunKey so it is a distinct, additive run.

shape.description:
Shape is the classified image shape (prose/conversation/social_post/
tabular/creative); ClassifyConfidence is the model's self-reported
confidence in it.

connect_supported.description:
ConnectSupported records whether Ogen can OAuth-redirect connect this
platform. false documents the Bluesky-style app-password exclusion as data
rather than code.

enabled.description:
Enabled is the operator soft on/off switch. A disabled platform
drops from GET /api/platforms and blocks new connects, but already-scheduled
posts still publish (the publish path resolves zernio_id regardless).

post_type_canvases.description:
PostTypeCanvases is the recommended artwork size per media-bearing
post-type slug, surfaced on the post-type rules (composer hints, the
Figma plugin's board frames).

supported_post_types.description:
SupportedPostTypes is the Zernio-publishable subset of PostTypes' slugs
— replaces SupportedPlatform.SupportedPostTypes. PostTypes carries
every slug for display; this array marks which ones actually publish.

zernio_id.description:
ZernioID is the Zernio wire slug ("twitter", "linkedin", …). It replaces
the retired Go registry's sqidToZernioID map: the publish path
and connect flow resolve this off the row. "" means the operator has not
yet assigned a slug (the row is not publishable until they do).

brand_voice_id.description:
Brand bindings: this post's own voice/audience. Nullable —
resolution falls back to the campaign's, then the workspace default /
legacy prose. content_plan/draft_post stamp the voice; both are overridable
via PUT /api/posts/:id or the targeted /:id/brand. FK ON DELETE SET NULL.

campaign.description: Hydrated relations — not stored in the database.

cloned_from_post_id.description:
ClonedFromPostID links a clone back to the Post it was duplicated
from. Nil for posts created directly. `nullzero` sends
NULL (not "") so the lineage is a clean "has a source / does not".

content_format.description:
ContentFormat is the post's rhetorical shape, independent of its
container (PlatformPostType). Nil means no format, the normal case.

cover_url.description:
CoverURL is the public URL of the picture a post card leads with — its
first drawable attachment (see PostAttachmentRepository.CoverKeysByPostIDs).
Minted per response by the posts handler and never accepted on writes, so
unlike media_urls it cannot round-trip back into a PUT.

first_comment.description:
FirstComment is posted under the live post, FirstCommentDelayMinutes
after it publishes (0 = with the post). Empty means no comment.

first_comment_status.description:
The first comment's outcome, written by the publish workers only. Nil
status means no comment went out with this post (yet).

platform_id.description:
platform_id and platform_post_type are nullable so draft posts can
exist without a platform chosen up front. They become
required when the post moves out of "draft" — enforced by the
posts handler, not by the schema.

`nullzero` makes bun send NULL (not "") for empty values, which is
required for platform_id because the FK to platforms can't match
an empty string. We use it on platform_post_type too for symmetry.

published_url.description:
PublishedURL is the platform permalink for the live post, kept
as a first-class field so the front-end can render "View post" off the
post it already has, without an analytics round-trip. Set from
the publisher's canonical URL on publish/verify, or accepted on PUT for
the Zernio skip path. `nullzero` sends NULL (not "") when unset; a URL
with an empty PublisherPostID is a user-supplied (unverified) link.

publisher.description:
Publisher integration fields (CON-69 §6/§7, generalized to
publisher-agnostic names in CON-93 §14).
Publisher marks which publisher adapter owns the external identity
(matches publishers.Publisher.ID(), e.g. "zernio"); empty until a
post is published through a publisher.
PublisherPostID is the id the publisher assigns when a Post is
submitted; the UNIQUE index in the migration prevents accidental
double-submit and is the join key into publisher analytics.
PublisherStatus mirrors the publisher's enum verbatim so the polling
task can short-circuit on already-handled terminal states.
PublishedResults carries the publisher's per-platform outcomes (URLs,
platform IDs) once the post resolves.
FailureReason distinguishes a publisher-reported failure from
reconciliation timeout — see CON-69 §8.

series_id.description:
SeriesID is the series that produced the post. It survives the series
being deleted (series are soft-deleted).

social_account_id.description:
SocialAccountID names which same-platform account this post
publishes to. NULL when unspecified — the submit worker
then auto-selects the platform's single account, or fails
`account_selection_required` when the platform has more than one.
`nullzero` sends NULL (not "") so the FK to social_accounts holds.

thread_segments.description:
ThreadSegments holds the ordered messages of a threaded post,
used only when PlatformPostType == PostTypeThread: index 0 is the root,
1..N-1 the ordered replies. Empty [] for every other post. Content
mirrors segment 0 so thread-unaware readers (quality CON-184, listings,
campaign summaries CON-152, analytics title) keep working; writes that
set segments restamp Content from the root. Per-segment media is carried
by PostAttachment.SegmentIndex, not here.

input_hash.description:
InputHash fingerprints the assessment inputs (rendered prompt + model)
so the assess flow skips re-running the model when nothing the model
sees has changed.

account_id.description:
AccountID is the login identity this session authenticates. The
session belongs to the account; UserID + TenantID are the active membership
/ default workspace it currently resolves to.

token_expires_at.description:
Health snapshot. Populated by the detect_expiring_connections
sweep from Zernio's GET /v1/accounts/health; all nullable and NULL until
the first sweep. TokenExpiresAt is the forward-looking token expiry that
drives the "connection expiring" owner notification; HealthStatus is
Zernio's healthy/warning/error verdict. Kept out of the reconciler's
upsert set so a sync never overwrites them. UnhealthySince marks the start
of the current unhealthy episode (NULL while healthy) and anchors the
notify-once dedupe.

bbox.description:
Bbox is the normalized image region a block was extracted from,
Kind == "image". A pointer so a nil bbox is omitted while a present one is
always serialized in full (all four coords, incl. legitimate 0 origins).

start_ms.description:
StartMs/EndMs bound an audio transcript chunk on the ORIGINAL asset
timeline, Kind == "time". Provenance marks how the anchor was
derived (e.g. "transcript", "image_extraction"). Empty for non-audio,
non-image anchors.

deleted_at.description:
DeletedAt marks a soft-deleted workspace. Membership
resolution filters it out, so a deleted workspace can't be listed, switched
to, or entered — but the row survives for support-side recovery. Plain
timestamp, NOT a bun `,soft_delete` column: see the migration comment.

first_comment_per_post_type.description:
FirstCommentPerPostType overrides MaxFirstCommentChars per slug; 0
turns the first comment off for that type (e.g. stories).

max_content_chars.description:
MaxContentChars is the default body-text ceiling applied to every post
type that PerPostType doesn't override. 0 = unbounded.

max_first_comment_chars.description:
MaxFirstCommentChars caps a post's first comment. 0 = the platform
takes no first comment.

max_title_chars.description:
MaxTitleChars caps the title on platforms with a distinct title field
(YouTube, LinkedIn article). 0 = no separate title limit.

per_post_type.description:
PerPostType overrides MaxContentChars for specific post-type slugs —
e.g. LinkedIn {"article": 100000} while its feed posts stay at 3000.

role.description:
Role is the account's authority in this tenant. Users that predate
invitations are 'owner' (each was the sole member of its tenant).

tenant.description:
Tenant is loaded only on demand (e.g. GET /api/current_user via
UserRepository.GetByIDWithTenant) and omitted otherwise, so ordinary
user responses stay unchanged. CON-97.

requires_video_title.description:
RequiresVideoTitle blocks publishing a video post whose title is empty.
A product rule for YouTube, where an untitled upload would be titled from
the description's first line or "Untitled Video"; feed/Reel platforms
have no separate title, so this stays false for them.

key.description: status string / platform id / post-type slug

label.description: human label (platform name; else the key or "None")

unassignedPhasePostCount.description: UnassignedPhasePostCount counts posts with no phase (or a stale phase id).

goal.description:
Goal is the CON-182 post-rate goal progress, or null when the campaign has
no goal configured (no positive estimated_post_count).

startDate.description:
StartDate/EndDate are the phase's effective window (YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive)
from the campaign's phase plan; null when the campaign is undated.

max_first_comment_chars.description:
MaxFirstCommentChars caps the post type's first comment; 0 means the
type takes none and the composer hides the field.

max_content_chars.description:
MaxContentChars is the body-text ceiling for this post type, resolved
from the platform's TextConstraints (per-post-type override, else the
platform default). nil means unbounded — the UI shows no counter cap.
Counts are Unicode code points, matching the server-side check.

requires_link.description:
RequiresLink marks a post type that publishes a target URL (cta_url)
the network unfurls into a preview card; the publish gate rejects an
empty or malformed one.

segmented.description:
Segmented marks a post type whose composer authors an ordered list of
messages rather than one body (the "thread" type). MaxContentChars
then carries the PER-SEGMENT limit (X 280 / Threads 500), and the UI renders
the segmented composer with a counter per message. false for every other type.

segment.description:
Segment names the 0-based thread message a failure belongs to,
so the composer can highlight the offending message. nil for whole-post
failures and every non-thread post.

PluginToken.description: "Bearer ogp_…" plugin token collected through the plugin pairing flow.
PluginToken.name: Authorization
